verdict.root_cause: At 10:52:03Z — about two minutes before onset — platform-automation updated the shippingservice container image reference to ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:v1.2.1-adservice, an artifact belonging to a different service, and unlike the four earlier update/revert cycles this one was never reverted [tr_1cb128a4a1c2]. From roughly 10:52:25 onward the shipping-service log stream contains only JVM/OpenTelemetry-javaagent process-startup sequences repeating at short intervals, with the earlier Rust-style request-handling logger gone and no GetQuote or ShipOrder handling at all [tr_805b5a83eb83] — i.e. the wrong (Java) artifact is starting under the shippingservice identity and never serving the shipping gRPC surface. Consequently every checkoutservice call to hipstershop.ShippingService/GetQuote fails fast (0.4–2.4ms) with no server-side child span, and that single erroring child terminates PlaceOrder and propagates to the frontend root [tr_9ad90e426eb5]. checkoutservice itself is healthy: no changes recorded against it [tr_8b49d40eb91d], no error-ratio departure from baseline [tr_0cb74cf61e9e], no error lines and continued order acceptance, but with the payment/email/queue-write completion steps missing after the onset [tr_55c59e9f5ddd] — the signature of a caller blocked at an upstream step, not an origin of failure. The downstream alerts (accounting, email, frauddetection, quote) follow from orders never reaching the payment/queue stages and from shippingservice no longer calling quoteservice.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on shippingservice as the failing element rather than the alerting checkoutservice. (1) Timing and artifact identity: the only unreverted change anywhere near onset is an image reference set to an adservice-tagged build on shippingservice at 10:52:03, two minutes before the 10:54:30 alert [tr_1cb128a4a1c2]. (2) Runtime evidence that the running artifact is not the shipping binary: the log stream switches from Rust-style request handling to repeating JVM/javaagent startup groups with zero request handling after 10:52:25 [tr_805b5a83eb83]. (3) Caller-side evidence of the mechanism: GetQuote client spans error in all ten sampled traces with no server-side counterpart, sub-3ms, consistent with connection-level rejection rather than a deadline, and every other checkout dependency (cart/Redis, currency, product catalog, feature flags) completes cleanly [tr_9ad90e426eb5]. checkoutservice is exonerated by its empty change log [tr_8b49d40eb91d], flat error ratio versus baseline [tr_0cb74cf61e9e], and absence of any diagnostic error while it keeps accepting orders [tr_55c59e9f5ddd]. The failing mechanism is that the artifact in place is not the one that should be running, which is bad_deploy; the fix is to restore the correct shippingservice image, not to restart the wrong one. shippingservice metrics contributed nothing either way — the counter is absent in both windows, a collection gap that predates the incident [tr_a8b5ce8362bc].
open_questions: No dispatch confirmed what the correct/prior shippingservice image reference was; the change record shows 'None -> ghcr.io/.../demo:v1.2.1-adservice', so the rollback target has to be recovered from deployment config rather than from this evidence.

Why the process restarts repeatedly is not established — the startup sequences complete with no exception, parse error, or fatal line [tr_805b5a83eb83], so whether it is a crash loop, a liveness-probe kill against a service that never opens the shipping port, or something else is unknown.

Log coverage for shippingservice is missing roughly 10:24:44–10:52:25, and checkoutservice logs skip the minutes on either side of 10:54:30 [tr_805b5a83eb83, tr_55c59e9f5ddd], so the precise transition from healthy to failing was never directly observed.

The declared checkoutservice dependencies other than shippingservice were never checked for changes (radius=seed, hops=0) [tr_8b49d40eb91d]; a concurrent change elsewhere cannot be excluded, only made unnecessary as an explanation.
quoteservice, emailservice, accountingservice and frauddetectionservice were never dispatched on; their alerts are inferred to be downstream consequences, not verified as such.

The change record is attributed to platform-automation on a repeating set/revert cycle [tr_1cb128a4a1c2]; whether the automation will re-apply or self-revert the image, and whether it must be paused before a manual rollback holds, is unsettled.

alternatives.root_cause: The shippingservice process is being killed and restarted for exceeding a memory or CPU limit, and the quote failures are a symptom of an unavailable, thrashing process rather than of the wrong artifact.
alternatives.why_not: Nothing in the evidence shows an OOM kill, limit breach, or resource metric; the restart pattern begins within ~20 seconds of the image reference change [tr_1cb128a4a1c2, tr_805b5a83eb83], and the log stream changes runtime family (Rust to JVM), which a resource kill of the correct binary would not explain.

alternatives.root_cause: A misconfigured QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR pointing shippingservice at an unresolvable quote host is what breaks GetQuote.
alternatives.why_not: That variable was set at 10:29:46Z and reverted at 10:41:27Z with no later re-application, so it was out of effect ~13 minutes before onset [tr_1cb128a4a1c2]; it also predicts a served-but-erroring GetQuote handler, whereas traces show no server-side shipping span at all [tr_9ad90e426eb5] and logs show no request handling [tr_805b5a83eb83].

proposal.expected_effect: Redeploying shippingservice at its pre-10:52:03Z image should restore the Rust shipping binary: the shipping-service log stream stops the repeating JVM/javaagent startup sequences and resumes INFO GetQuoteRequest/ShipOrder handling lines as at 10:24:36; checkoutservice traces show a server-side shippingservice child under hipstershop.ShippingService/GetQuote with no STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and frontend roots stop inheriting the error. Note shippingservice's own error-ratio series is empty in both windows, so confirmation must come from logs and caller-side traces, not target metrics.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if after 5 minutes the JVM startup sequences still repeat (wrong prior tag recovered, or platform-automation re-applied the adservice image), or if GetQuote spans still error with a healthy-looking Rust shipping process running — which would mean the mechanism is not the image swap. Also unresolved: the change record shows 'None -> ...', so the correct prior tag must be read from deployment config before executing; if no prior tag exists there, this action's precondition is not met and it should not be run.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is wrong, this is a needless container recreate that drops shipping in-process state and extends the outage by the recreate duration. If the automation cycle re-applies the bad image, the rollback flaps and the service restarts repeatedly. Rolling back to a stale tag could reintroduce an older shipping defect.
proposal.blast_radius: shippingservice only. During recreate, checkoutservice sees GetQuote/ShipOrder connection resets, which propagates to frontend as failed PlaceOrder; quoteservice sees shipping's outbound traffic return. Recovery of orders reaching payment/queue stages should relieve the accounting, email and frauddetection alerts.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Checkout alerts first, then its downstream consumers fan out minutes later, which is consistent with a checkout-centric failure rather than a benign blip. No open incidents to fold this into and the pattern is not dismissible, so it warrants specialists; the trigger (deploy, config, or a dependency) is not yet distinguishable.
